doc.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Deaths of Woody Shaw, Carter Jefferson and Clint Houston
summary: He relays secondhand accounts of Shaw's fatal accident and Jefferson's death abroad, and notes Houston has also died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: He had a terrible accident, didn’t he?

He had a terrible accident where he was invited by Max Roach to come to the Vanguard. He was staying with his parents. The limo came to pick him up. Now this is kind of sketchy because I’m getting all this second hand. The limo comes, picks him up, brings him to the Vanguard. He’s going around the club and he’s kind of loud and the club ain’t but that big. So they decided he needs to be sent home. He gave the limo driver a hard time coming, so the limo driver said listen, I’m out of here, you take care of him. So they had to get him a cab. But no one went with him. He went by himself. So he commandeered, I think he commandeered the cab to a location he wanted to go to. All right? What happened in between that I really don’t know because only Woody knows. Next thing you know he is on a railroad track. The train comes in the station and goes over his arm. And he is in trauma, and I think they amputate the arm, and a few more weeks of that, he finally succumbed. And then Carter Jefferson was in Europe or Poland. And he had a problem with his liver or something like that. He took sick. The promoters thought he was high on drugs. There was no ambulance, they had to put him in a cab and drive him miles to the hospital. And they left him on the front step. Because they didn’t want to be hooked up with this. You know what I’m saying? They didn’t want to be a party to a possible drug situation.
Right, in a foreign country and the whole thing.
